alt: The tiered stone arcades of the El Jem Roman amphitheatre under a blue sky
caption: El Jem amphitheatre, built around AD 238 for roughly 35,000 spectators, stands almost intact in a small market town. On Day 5 the group visits it at opening time, before the tour buses, and can walk the arcades and underground passages.

alt: Ruined Roman houses with sunken rooms, stairways and columns at Bulla Regia
caption: Bulla Regia in the north-west is where wealthy Romans built their living rooms underground to escape summer heat. On Day 3 the group walks down into these cool, mosaic-floored rooms, the first major site after collecting the car.

alt: The columned Capitol of Dougga seen from the Roman theatre above olive fields
caption: The Capitol of Dougga, seen from the Roman theatre, crowns a hillside town among olive groves. It is the best-preserved Roman small town in North Africa and the main stop of Day 4, reached by a short drive from Bulla Regia.

alt: A sunken courtyard of a troglodyte house at Matmata with doorways cut into the surrounding walls
caption: A troglodyte courtyard at Matmata: families dug rooms around an open pit to stay cool in summer and warm in winter. The group spends the night of Day 5 in one of these pit houses and explores more on Day 6.

alt: Rocky hill landscape around the Amazigh village of Toujane in the Matmata range
caption: The stony hills around Toujane, an Amazigh village in the Matmata range. On Day 6 the route winds through them from Tamezret, giving a first sense of the dry upland country before the desert.

alt: Pale sand and low dunes at the desert edge near Douz
caption: The sand edge near Douz, the gateway to the Grand Erg Oriental dune sea. On Day 7 a guided 4x4 takes the group in for a night in tents, the wild-camping highlight of the trip.

location: Chott el Djerid, between Kebili and Tozeur
alt: Mirage over the white salt flat of the Chott el Djerid
caption: A mirage shimmers over the white salt crust of the Chott el Djerid, which the road crosses on a causeway between Kebili and Tozeur. The crossing on Day 8 follows a sunrise in the dunes and is one of the trip's strangest landscapes.

commonsFile: File:Great Mosque of Kairouan minaret view 01.jpg
alt: The square minaret rising above the courtyard of the Great Mosque of Kairouan
caption: The square minaret of the Great Mosque of Kairouan, founded in 670 and the oldest place of worship in the Maghreb. It is the cultural stop of Day 4-5 and one of the few major mosques where the courtyard can be visited.

alt: Stacked vaulted ghorfa storage rooms around a courtyard in Medenine
caption: The ghorfas of Medenine are barrel-vaulted granaries stacked around courtyards by Amazigh tribes. Day 10 passes through them on the way from the Chott to the coast, showing the fortified-storage tradition of the south.

alt: Panorama of Tamezret, a ridge-top Amazigh village in the Matmata hills
caption: Tamezret, a ridge-top Amazigh village of the Matmata mountains, still has stone lanes and one of the few places where Tamazight is spoken daily. The group walks there on Day 6 between the pit houses and Toujane.

alt: Colonnaded courtyard of the Zitouna Mosque in the medina of Tunis
caption: The Zitouna Mosque courtyard in the heart of the Tunis medina. The evening and morning walks of Days 1-2 pass through the souk lanes around it, a gentle introduction to the country before the road trip.

alt: Ruins and standing arches of the Antonine Baths at Carthage beside the sea
caption: The Antonine Baths at Carthage, among the largest Roman baths ever built, stand beside the Mediterranean. Day 2 visits them on the way from the medina, before the group collects the car.

alt: Market stalls and whitewashed arcades in Houmt Souk on Djerba
caption: The market of Houmt Souk, the main town of Djerba. Day 12 is kept free here to wander the lanes and workshops at the end of the loop.

commonsFile: File:Une grappe de datte avant la récolte , palmeraie de tozeur - tunisie.jpg
location: Palm grove of Tozeur, Tozeur Governorate
alt: A cluster of dates ripening on a palm in the Tozeur oasis
caption: Date clusters ripening in the Tozeur palm grove. Day 9 is spent walking the shaded irrigation channels of this oasis after the salt-flat crossing, and doubles as a buffer day.
